question: Should browser page navigation reject HTTP(S) URLs with embedded username/password userinfo before dispatch, or preserve URL-embedded Basic auth with stronger redaction?
rationale: Fail-fast rejection improves credential safety but breaks a previously accepted URL form, so automation can identify the implementation gap but cannot choose the security/compatibility policy for existing users.

options.title: Reject and redact before dispatch
options.body: Treat URL-embedded browser navigation credentials as unsupported, block them before any local/proxy/browser boundary, redact surfaced diagnostics, and document supported auth alternatives.

options.title: Preserve Basic-auth URLs with stronger redaction
options.body: Keep URL-embedded Basic auth usable while hardening logs and errors, accepting that credentialed URLs still reach the browser runtime path.

options.title: Defer to broader browser auth design
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers choose a dedicated browser-auth alternative such as profiles, cookies, headers, or Playwright credentials.

recommendation.title: Reject and redact before dispatch
recommendation.body: Treat URL-embedded browser navigation credentials as unsupported, block them before any local/proxy/browser boundary, redact surfaced diagnostics, and document supported auth alternatives.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser plugin history and current assignment point to steipete as the strongest available routing owner for this policy-sensitive browser behavior.
